1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4.name: Scotch Game: Scotch Gambit, Dubois Réti Defence

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5..strategy: The modern way to play the gambit: the pawn gains space and drives the knight away, so White is not forced to give up e4. Black keeps the extra pawn on d4 for now, but has to spend time on the knight while White's pieces come out with tempo.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5..name: Scotch Game: Scotch Gambit, Advance Variation
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5..background: Often adopted by Evgeny Sveshnikov, this line has gradually become the main line of the Open Variation.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5..strategy: The traditional gambit: White castles and lets Black take e4 for development and pressure down the open e-file. Black's best reply, taking the pawn, gives material back for a level game, so this is sound but offers White little more than equality.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5..name: Italian Game: Scotch Gambit

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5..strategy: A tricky second attack on f7 while the pawn still stands on d4. It moves a piece twice and leaves e4 undefended, and Black's counter in the centre forces White to give up castling and to defend, so White is the one who has to be careful.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5..name: Italian Game: Two Knights Defence, Perreux Variation

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5..strategy: Hits the c4-bishop with a pawn, so White cannot simply regain the pawn on d4 and has to find a good square for the bishop, while the e5-pawn still attacks the knight. The most natural and common answer: Black keeps the extra pawn and fights for the centre.

Steps away from the pawn and hits e5 a second time, with the knight on g4 as well as the one on c6, while eyeing f2. The knight is far from home and f7 is left to the king alone, so it is playable but rarely best; White has to defend e5 and then use the tempo.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5..name: Scotch Game: Scotch Gambit, Kingside Variation

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5..strategy: The best reply: Black takes the second pawn and the centre pawns White offered are gone. White's compensation is development and the open e-file, but Black gives material back to settle the position and reaches a comfortable, level game.

Builds a pawn wall and opens the c8-bishop instead of grabbing e4, but it leaves the d4-pawn to be won back at once and gives White the freer pieces. Solid but second-rate: Black has not made use of the extra pawn.
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5..name: Italian Game: Scotch Gambit, Janowski Defence

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bc4 Nf6 4.d4 exd4 5..strategy: Develops the bishop to its most active square, defends the extra pawn on d4 and aims at f2. It invites the sharp e5 that White is hoping for and reaches a heavily analysed attack by transposition, so Black is theoretically fine but has to walk a narrow path.
A modest developing move that prepares to castle and leaves the d4-pawn to White's recapture. Black stays solid and safe but passive, and hands White the freer development.
